title: A continuous function equal to one at zero stays above one half nearby
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous with $f(0) = 1$. Then there is $\delta > 0$ such that $f(x) > 1/2$ for every $x$ with $|x| < \delta$.

steps.text: Since $f$ is continuous at $0$, for $\varepsilon = 1/2$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that $|f(x) - f(0)| < 1/2$ for all $x$ with $|x - 0| < \delta$.
fragment: obtain ⟨δ, hδ, h⟩ := Metric.continuous_iff.mp hf 0 (1 / 2) (by norm_num)

steps.text: Take this $\delta$, and let $|x| < \delta$. Then $|f(x) - 1| < 1/2$, because $f(0) = 1$.
fragment: have hx' : |f x - 1| < 1 / 2 := by simpa [Real.dist_eq, h0] using h x (by simpa [Real.dist_eq] using hx)

fragment: obtain ⟨δ, hδ, h⟩ : ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x y : ℝ, dist x y < δ → dist (f x) (f y) < 1 / 2 := Metric.continuous_iff.mp hf 0 (1 / 2) (by norm_num)

steps.text: Take this $\delta$, and let $|x| < \delta$. Applying it with $y = 0$ gives $|f(x) - 1| < 1/2$, because $f(0) = 1$.
fragment: have hx' : |f x - 1| < 1 / 2 := by simpa [Real.dist_eq, h0] using h x 0 (by simpa [Real.dist_eq] using hx)
